subject: Agriculture
title: GMOs: Promise and Fear
description: A quick, practical guide to GMOs: Promise and Fear.

hook.text: Bt cotton produces its own insecticide inside every cell. Bollworms eat it and die—no spraying needed.

buildup.text: Genetic engineering inserts specific genes from one organism into another—bacteria genes into plants, for example.

discovery.text: GM crops reduced insecticide use by 37% and increased yields by 22% in developing countries, per meta-analyses.

twist.text: Public fear persists despite scientific consensus on safety. The EU effectively bans GM crop cultivation.

climax.text: The GM debate is less about science and more about corporate control, trust, and cultural values.

punchline.text: The science is settled. The politics never will be.

quiz.question: By how much did GM crops reduce insecticide use according to meta-analyses?
